title: A Bride's Story
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: In a town near the Caspian Sea in the late 19th century, 20-year-old Amir, an archer and rider from a semi-nomadic tribe, is married to 12-year-old Karluk. The story follows their household and other young brides along the Silk Road, including English traveler Henry Smith, as Russian expansion and tribal conflict press on their lives.
life_message: It holds up family, craft, hospitality and patient love within a living tradition.

content.note: Tribal raids and battles; Amir's kin attack the town; a death in battle (Wikipedia; AniList War signal).
Sieges and threat to families, mostly calm iyashikei tone (AniList Iyashikei).
Married couples; one chaste kiss between Amir and Karluk (ANN); some bathing and wedding-night scenes reported (to verify).
Period pipes or drink possible (to verify).
Grief and worry, no self-harm noted.
Marriage of a 12-year-old shown as normal custom of the setting; ANN calls the age gap a possible deterrent.

delivery.note: Family and craft are shown through household life, with clans who treat daughters as bargaining chips as the contrast.

winners_losers: Families who keep faith with each other, like the Eihon household, win; clans who treat daughters as bargaining chips and expanding empires lose sympathy. Traditional community life gets the sympathy.
